structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E052. The tip is E049: 5.198 s and 0.7535; its rebuild E050 read 0.7552 at 5.206 s. The tip is E036 plus an annealed group-2 freeze (LR annealed over 75–90%, frozen for the last 10%) plus +0.25 epoch, about 237 steps.

1. Noise. Rebuilds of one commit move the 3-seed mean with an SD of about 0.2 pp (E036: 0.7532/0.7525/0.7497/0.7544; E049: 0.7535/0.7552). Time reproduces to about ±0.02 s. Any lever that costs ≥0.1 pp is close to a coin flip at the 0.753 gate, so my bands are about ±0.3 pp.

2. Weight decay acts only through the SGD groups. muon_update renormalizes the filters and applies no wd, so filter wd is inert (H1.5.4 is settled by reading the code). The optimum is near ×0.5.

3. Annealed freezes are the best lever. A frozen block skips its memory-bound BN/GELU backward, its dgrad, its Muon NS and the optimizer traffic, so it saves 1.5–2× its FLOP share: about 7.7 ms per step for group 1 and about 10 ms for group 2 (E028, E046). An idea nobody has proposed: a frozen block is not truly frozen. Lookahead lerps every param, so frozen fast weights keep getting pulled toward the EMA, and train-mode BN keeps adapting the statistics. The "freeze" is therefore an averaging-only phase. That explains why a gentle late freeze is close to free and costs about the same as the LR anneal it replaces. It is not free once the frozen block has not yet adapted to the final 32 px distribution. Before that point the dose cost grows superlinearly (E037's cliff at 60%).

4. Steps carry accuracy; early pixels do not. E026 and E033 were free. Removing steps or samples (E031, E040, E041, E048) costs about the dial rate, 1.2–1.8 s/pp. E052 is the exception: selection plus a top-up read 0.7555 at 4.99 s on seeds 0–2 but was discarded, presumably on the held-out pairing. Selection net of the top-up is roughly zero, with noisy upside.

5. How training ends is at a tuned local optimum. Every change to the averaging, the loss or BN recalibration lost 0.2–0.5 pp (E025, E030, E032, E044).

6. Stem architecture matters more than its FLOPs suggest. The strided conv (E051) cost 0.9 pp for 0.29 s. ReLU in place of GELU should save 1.5–3% at a 0.2–0.4 pp cost, which is worse than the dial.

7. Intermittent stem gradients: Muon orthogonalizes the update, so a half-rate update roughly halves group 1's effective LR in the 28 px phase. That should land between E037's full freeze and no freeze, costing about 0.1–0.25 pp for about 0.2 s, near the dial rate.

8. Unexploited levers with identical math: lazy per-epoch augmentation (the last epoch augments 50k images for about 13 steps) and skipping the Lookahead traffic on frozen params. Together they are worth about 1–2%.

9. Transfer to the PCIe judge: times about 5–10% higher, with the ranking unchanged. The real risk is a population mean of about 0.753 against the 0.75 bar.

Unsure:
- whether the 70% anneal start for group 2 crosses a cliff;
- whether seeds 13–32 are harder or the gap is winner's curse;
- where the rebuild variance comes from (autotune vs atomics).

forecasts.reason: About 12 more frozen steps at ~10 ms each saves ~0.12 s, but an anneal that starts at the 32 px switch gives group 2 no time to adapt at 32 px, so a ~0.15 pp loss is likely, worse than the dial.
Same recipe as I082: about 0.12 s saved for an expected loss of about 0.1–0.2 pp, a milder version of E037's cliff.
About 35 truncated 28 px steps at ~5 ms saved each gives ~0.17 s. Halving group 1's effective Muon LR mid-run probably costs ~0.15 pp, near the dial rate and within noise.
About 9 more frozen steps saves ~0.06 s, too small to resolve. Two steps at 32 px are likely too few to adapt, so expect a small loss.
The fused kernels are bytes-bound and ReLU's saved tensor cuts the reads only partly. The projected saving is probably under 3%, so the branch closes, or a run shows a 0.2 pp loss.
The cuts are near-dial trades, and the top-up refunds roughly what they cost. The net is about −1.5 to −2.5% time at a flat mean, so the gate is a coin flip.

cruxes: Does a frozen block's accuracy neutrality come from Lookahead and train-mode BN still adapting it (the 'averaging-only phase' mechanism)? Test: freeze group 2 and also exclude its params from the Lookahead lerp. If accuracy drops, the mechanism holds, and freeze doses before the 32 px switch will cliff.

Why was E052 (selection plus top-up, 4.99 s, 0.7555 on seeds 0–2) discarded? If it failed the held-out pairing by under 0.1 pp, then selection net of a top-up is the cheapest remaining lever, and stacking it matters more than any freeze-dose tweak.

How much train time sits outside the step graphs (augmenting the full final epoch, the Lookahead traffic on frozen params)? If it is ≥2%, the identical-math cuts dominate every accuracy-trading lever left.
